service.description: Import a data set, here (a ServiceJob runs it in the background). A run's scope is its source key (every data set sharing the sourceKey, which must share one format) and its country. Preflight, refused with an error and no run: the set registered and enabled; for a set downloaded from its URL, outside requests allowed (maps@external-requests) and no location given; for an operator's file (a set with no URL), a countryGeoId and a location under the user's own folder of dbresource://moqui/maps/import/ ((userId)/), runtime://import/ or the user's own uploads; the license acknowledged by an administrator (licenseAckUserId); no run of the same scope in progress (one whose row has not changed for an hour is taken as abandoned and marked failed, and a live one so marked stops at its next check). countryGeoId is needed for a set read a country at a time and must be its coverage for a set with one. A run downloads from the registered host (never an internal address) to runtime/tmp/geo-import as it arrives, within maps@import-max-bytes, conditionally on the edition in use's ETag and Last-Modified (an unchanged source ends the run GdiUnchanged); the edition in use is the scope's last completed run, and none while the source key has no rows in date there (after a Remove), so such a run fetches whole. It reads the whole file (a zip member within maps@import-max-bytes and a ratio limit, lines within 64 KB), checking each row's country, code shape (leading zeros kept, a partial code a declared prefix), computed IDs, coordinates and duplicates, writing nothing; refuses a file with no row to load, or with fewer than 80% of the edition in use's rows unless forced; loads in batches of 2,000 codes, a transaction each, creating or updating by computed ID and leaving unchanged rows alone, the counts written and the cancel flag read between batches. Only after a whole load, it end-dates (thruDate) what this source key owns in the run's country that the new edition does not have: its postal codes (but one another source still has a point for), place names and point associations, a row passed over for another fault keeping its code when the code could be read. The run (GdiCompleted, with its edition) is then the edition in use. A run that committed rows (a whole load, or the batches of one that failed or was cancelled after them) clears the postal lookup cache; a completed run of an upload deletes the uploads of its scope's earlier runs. A run never changes a row another source key owns, a code made by hand (no sourceKey), a user-confirmed point or a record's own location; it revives a code another source key owns and retired when this edition has it (the code stays that source's). Where two sources have a code each writes its own point, and the data set's priority makes the active one. Rejected rows go to the error file (dbresource://moqui/maps/geo-import/(userId)/(geoDataImportId)/errors.csv, as an ETL run's: the first 10,000, and how many more), the first 100 in errors; a failed run's errorLocation names the step. geoDataImportId runs a pending run (GdiPending, made by the screen or job that starts it), whose own data set and country are used; when the run is one of a queue (queueId, start#GeoDataImport's every country), it then starts the queue's next pending run as a run of the GeoDataImport ServiceJob, whatever its own end (one whose job does not start is marked failed and the next is tried); a refusal every run of the queue would meet (the set disabled or unreadable, its license, outside requests off, the size limit, the job's user refused or not authorized) instead cancels the queue's waiting runs with that reason. A ServiceJob with no user signed in names the user to run as in runAsUserId, a ServiceJobUser of the job who added themselves.

parameter.name: force
parameter.description: Fetch whatever the edition in use, and accept a file with far fewer rows than it

parameter.name: runAsUserId
parameter.description: For a ServiceJob run with no user signed in: the user to run as, a ServiceJobUser of the job who added themselves

service.description: Ask a run to stop: a pending run is cancelled at once; a running one reads the request between its steps and batches and ends GdiCancelled with nothing retired, the rows of the batches it loaded kept and the edition in use unchanged. A running one whose row has not changed for an hour is taken as abandoned and ended at once (and its queue goes on with its next). Refused for a run that has ended. With queueId instead, the whole queue of an import of every country: its pending runs cancelled at once (so none starts) and its running one asked to stop (ended at once when abandoned); refused when none is in progress. cancelledCount is the queue's runs cancelled or asked to stop.

Remove what a data set's source key owns, for countryGeoId (needed for a set read a country at a time; every country for a set with none), a batch of about 2,000 Geo IDs at a time, each batch in its own transaction: a batch's place names and point associations, then each point, postal code and county, place or city Geo it made that no row of any entity refers to (from the entity model's relationships to Geo, GeoPoint and GeoPostalCode: another source's points and place names, an address, a group); the rest are end-dated. A user-confirmed point stays, with its association, and keeps its Geo; a record's own location is left alone. For the ZCTA-to-county set, its county-to-code links are deleted, 2,000 a batch; a set of countries or divisions is refused, those rows being shared. A removal stopped part way leaves whole batches removed, and a Remove again finishes it. A batch that fails is rolled back and the removal goes on with the next; the error names the failed batches' Geo IDs. Refused while an import of the source key and country, or another removal of the set, is in progress: the removal marks the data set (removingStamp, removingCountryGeoId, touched before each batch, abandoned after an hour unchanged), and start#GeoDataImport and the import refuse the scope meanwhile; an import that starts anyway stops the removal before its next batch. rowsDeleted and rowsRetired count rows. When every batch is removed, the operator's uploads its runs read (under dbresource://moqui/maps/import/) are deleted; the postal lookup cache is cleared.

A typed postal code read by the importer's own country rules (moqui_lib::geo::postal), for the postal lookup (org.moqui.maps.MapServices.get#PostalLocation, which calls it as its own step): normalized (upper case, spaces and hyphens out, leading zeros kept), its display spelling and granularity, the declared prefix of a full Canadian, British or Dutch code, and a US ZIP+4 read as its ZIP code (zipPlus4). Text that is no code of the country answers reason alone. Reads and writes nothing.

What Maps › Configuration › Geo data shows: each registered data set with its license, attribution, coverage and whether it may be imported now (importRefusal: disabled, license not acknowledged, outside requests off for a download); the countries its source key has been imported for (a scope listed under the set its last run was of), each with its edition in use (the last completed run's), its postal codes and points in date and its last run; the last 50 runs with their counts, error file and failure; and the refresh schedule (the GeoDataRefresh ServiceJob's) and the conf limits. Changes nothing.

Record that the signed-in administrator acknowledged a data set's license and attribution terms (licenseAckUserId, in the audit log, and licenseAckDate): import#GeoData refuses a set whose license nobody acknowledged. Loading the seed again keeps it.

Start an import as a run of the GeoDataImport ServiceJob, never in the request: a pending run (GdiPending, the signed-in user's) that the job's import#GeoData takes, so it has a job run, its notification (topic GeoDataImport) and the run row from the start. Refused here, with no run: a set that is not there or is disabled, a license not acknowledged, a download while outside requests are off, no country for a set read a country at a time or an operator's file (or one its countryCodes do not list), no file for an operator's file, a run of the same source key and country in progress, and a removal of its rows under way (remove#GeoData's mark), each before an upload is written. An operator's file is an upload (file, at most maps@import-max-bytes, kept under dbresource://moqui/maps/import/(userId)/) or a location the importer allows. A refused job start leaves the run failed. everyCountry (a set read a country at a time) imports every country of its countryCodes that has a country Geo as a queue (plans/Maps.md §6.3): a pending run a country sharing a queueId (the first run's ID), refused while a run of the source key is in progress (one with no word for an hour not counted; the data set's row is locked so two starts do not both pass); only the first starts here, and each run starts the next when it ends (import#GeoData), one at a time, each its own run and edition; cancel#GeoDataImport with the queueId cancels the rest. everyCountryEstimate gives the confirmation's estimate.

parameter.name: countryGeoId
parameter.description: A Geo ID or an alpha-2 or alpha-3 code

parameter.name: again
parameter.description: A Refresh: an operator's file given no file or location is the file its scope's last run read

parameter.name: everyCountry
parameter.description: Every country of a set read a country at a time, as a queue of runs

service.description: Start the GeoDataRefresh ServiceJob now (Refresh all, and the maps.geodata.refresh RefreshOperation of System › Health), which imports again each scope in use (it ever completed a run and still has rows): a source that has not changed ends as current with a conditional request, so a refresh of unchanged sources changes nothing.

The GeoDataRefresh ServiceJob's run: import#GeoData again for each scope (a source key and country) in use: one that ever completed a run and still has rows in date (countries and divisions always have), whatever its last run, but one with a run in progress or of a disabled set, with the operator's file of its last run where it was one, one after another; a scope that fails is logged and counted and the rest go on. A scheduled run has no user: runAsUserId (the job's parameter, set by schedule#GeoDataRefresh) is the administrator import#GeoData runs as.

Schedule the GeoDataRefresh ServiceJob every week (Sunday 03:20) or every month (the 1st, 03:20), or stop its schedule (none, which pauses it). A schedule runs as the administrator who set it: they become a user of the job who added themselves (notified of each run) and its runAsUserId parameter.
